issue.description:
ADR-001 (Accepted, 2026-08-12) specifies post-0.1 item R025: a third dependency kind `verifies` so authors can declare the check relationship explicitly, plus a structural diagnosis — a `blocks` edge whose blocker `verifies` its blocked bead is reported as an inverted verification gate. Measured incidence in adjacent workspaces was 21–31 inverted edges (4–6% of new beads), an acyclic but semantically unexecutable ordering that cycles checks and readiness computation cannot catch. Requirements: extend the dependency schema, manifest, and checkpoint round-trip to the third kind; keep §3.4 cycle rejection intact across it; report the diagnosis (advisory only — never reject the edge at insert, never infer from titles); surface it in doctor output; update `bead schema explain` / field-guide content for the new kind. No open bead currently tracks R025. Verification: declaration round-trips through checkpoint export/import; diagnosis fires on a declared-inversion fixture and stays silent on legitimate baseline-gate orderings and on undeclared inversions; title-heuristic regression test asserts no inference from title text.

Created by: weave strand

issue.description: BR-T16 follow-up found during BR-T17 review. Native audit events are normally stored with NULL origin_store_uuid/origin_event_sequence and receive deterministic wire identities only during checkpoint export. The live secret scanner/redaction locator currently uses the nullable stored pair directly, so multiple native events share a selector and an UPDATE predicate can address more than one row. Implement a stable exact-row locator that derives or canonicalizes the event wire identity under the redaction IMMEDIATE transaction without changing public event identity/order; add tests for one and multiple native NULL-origin events, duplicate-looking findings, exact hash recomputation, rollback, replay, and checkpoint round-trip. Do not expose matched bytes.
issue.title: Canonicalize native event identity before historical redaction
